page: Amazon Web Services m8ine.2xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance virtualized on the AWS Nitro system. The configuration includes 8 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 4 physical Intel processor cores running at 3.9 GHz, with 2 threads enabled per core. System memory totals 32.0 GB, delivering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This structure maintains a classic balanced resource profile designed to serve standard computing tasks without an over-allocation of compute or memory capacity.

From an architectural perspective, the m8ine.2xlarge is built without integrated local storage or hardware acceleration. The instance provisions zero local disks and contains no GPU components, necessitating the use of remote Elastic Block Store volumes for operating systems, application code, and persistent data retention. Network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, ensuring reliable network throughput between networked storage targets, microservices, and external endpoints. Public IPv4 addressing is not bundled by default.

Because the platform relies solely on network-attached storage and standard general purpose resources, it provides predictable efficiency for workloads that do not demand physical NVMe storage latency or heavy parallel matrix processing. The 1:4 compute-to-RAM balance combined with dedicated multi-threading makes the m8ine.2xlarge appropriate for containerized web services, enterprise application runtimes, continuous integration workers, medium-scale relational databases backed by networked volumes, and general purpose microservices infrastructure.
description: Amazon Web Services m8ine.2xlarge is a general purpose instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. The virtual machine provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, coupled with 32 GB of system memory to maintain a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present. Storage requirements depend entirely on external network-attached volumes, as the instance offers no local SSD or NVMe disks. Networking capabilities feature a baseline throughput of 12 Gbps, offering sufficient interconnect speed for data transfer and communication within distributed environments. The combination of dedicated Intel processing units, balanced RAM allocation, and high-speed network integration delivers cost-efficient resource provisioning for non-disk-intensive applications, including microservices deployments, containerized application runtimes, continuous integration pipelines, web serving clusters, and distributed backend middleware.
